title: Me gusta la comida española
blurbEn: You have used 'me gusta' since Unit 1. Here is what it is actually doing — and why it becomes 'gustan' when there is more than one thing.
body:
Me gusta mucho la comida española. Es muy buena y no es difícil.

Me gustan las verduras y el pescado. Mi plato favorito es el arroz con verduras.

A mi hermana no le gusta el pescado. Ella prefiere la carne.

A mis padres les gusta todo. Ellos comen de todo y nunca dicen que no.

¿Y a ti? ¿Qué comida te gusta más?
translationEn:
I like Spanish food a lot. It is very good and not difficult.

I like vegetables and fish. My favourite dish is rice with vegetables.

My sister does not like fish. She prefers meat.

My parents like everything. They eat everything and never say no.

And you? What food do you like most?

gustan.note: Plural, because 'las verduras' is plural. The food is the subject, not you.

le.note: 'A mi hermana no le gusta' — the 'a mi hermana' and the 'le' both point at the same person. Spanish says it twice.

phrases.note: Literally 'they please me'. The verb agrees with the thing liked, never with you.
